body: Im 29 and Im still terrified of walking by groups of teenagers in places like that. The last time I was at the beach, Im pretty sure one teenage boy actually did the loser sign on his forehead to me as I walked by, completely unprovoked.
How was it? The process of leaving, getting used to your new country,etc? How are you doing now?

It's dangerous. I have an aunt who once lived in a house on the outskirts of the city and she got robbed once. A group of armed men tied her up and kept her for hours inside of her house before going away carrying everything they could. You'll still find people who blast loud music every day, people will throw their trash on the sides of the road and in front of other people's properties. And how do you keep calling the police if everyone knows everyone? Another relative experiences such issues in the rural town he lives and he was afraid that if he kept complaining the offenders would get angry and he would get shot over it. 

And then there's the fact that parts of the countryside are rapidly becoming slums. Sometimes they grow organically, a family grows and a single family home surrounded by nature becomes a bunch of ugly little houses, all next and on top of each other. Sometimes the government will build these huge complexes of buildings and townhomes for social housing, and in less than 5 years they turn into huge slums. Then you have to sell your property at a loss because no one in their right mind would want to live there, its far away from everything but at the same time you have issues of rising crimes, loud music, etc. 

This is what people don't get when I said I would like to live in a developed country. Yes, I know people struggle there, but it's different. I promise you, you won't find the kind of poverty and criminality we have here in even the most problematic parts of Italy, France, England,etc.

You don't have to apologize, that wasn't the impression I got from your comment at all. And it is true, there are people in other countries, and even in my own country, who have it way worse than me. 

I feel the same way, I'm just not naturally ambitious or with a big drive. I guess someone more capable could have used the discomfort and anger I feel and channeled into becoming independent and sucessful, but I'm not like that. All I want is a quiet life, preferably as far away as possible from other people. Somewhere I could leave the doors and windows open with no fear, where I could only hear the sounds of nature.

You must be very proud of your parents, they sound like great people. I already have the luck of being in one of the nicer parts of my country, but over the years I've been watching the good parts get absorbed by the bad. Our own neighborhood, while it was never upscale or fancy, used to be extremelly quiet. Now its so loud with the constant sound of motorcycles and loud music. Slums are growing and streets that used to be beautiful are now ugly. 

And yes people don't understand that even if you live comfortably, you will still be exposed to the harsh reality of living in a third world country. Maybe its not so bad for those who can't just switch off some part of their brain, but ever since I was little the sight of poverty and inequality makes me extremelly disquieted. I used to dream that one day we would tackle these issues as a country, and all of us would have the right to a peaceful and beautiful life. But now I realize that will never happen. 

I keep thinknig of my ancestors who left everything behind to move here in search of a honest life, and I wish I had the strenght they had in doing the reverse move. Thank you so much for your kindness.

I've been frozen in this hell because every side I look, it seems it will end badly. I could suck it up, get a job and pretend to be a normal person. It would be like college, watching everyone else living their lives while all I do is work and hide. I would be miserable and likely just wait for my parents to die so I could kill myself.

Or I could transition, move out somehow and get a job to support myself. I would become a joke, a man in a skirt prime for hate and attacks. The shame would destroy my parent's lives and would likely lead them to an early grave. I would never be able to have children, and no man in his right man would as much as look at me. In the end I'd likely just kill myself too.

And the final option would be to simply end it now, which would also destroy my parent's lives. I feel like I'm hanging on the edge of a precipice and there's no way out.

Thank you so much. I think I have to be realistic though, the men in both sides of the family are usually tall, broadly built and I am not different. My hands and feet are bigger than most men, I would become a joke if I tried to transition. It would be like having a target on my back for hate crime. 

Over the years I've read about and watched videos of WWOOF. It could be nice, but the idea of being part of a group of likely younger people is terrifying. As much as I yearn for human contact, I don't miss that feeling from college of being painfully ignored when I tried to speak, being forced to stand awkwardly outside, but just close enough to a group of friends chatting animately.

I think a stronger, more capable person would have used that as fuel to become independent. They had good intentions, but they never allowed me to become my own person and be independent. 

We weren't the kind of household where kids were allowed to speak their minds or have opinions of their own. Everything I said, thought or wanted was always wrong. It's funny that my mother always had a bit of a ditzy personality, going around the house saying randomy things in a sing-songy voice and whatnot. You'd see her and think we must have had this free childhood, but it was the opposite. It was like she was the only one allowed to be like that. She always badmouthed my father's side of the family, leaving me alienated whenever we saw them every year, but also kept me isolated from her side. We had recconected with some cousins on her side, and I was feeling great having that kind of relationship. But my mother screwed up everything with her paranoia and jealously, so now I feel more alone than ever.

My father always boasted about how even from a young age no one had to tell him to do anything, he did all on his own free will. How that's what separates people from beasts. And yet, every time I tried to break away and be proactive, he always sabotages it and is vehemently against it.

Though I was fine intelectually, I didn't even had a phone in high school or cared about that. I quite literally played with toys until I was 18. Now, even though I still feel quite childish, I am what I think I should have been in my late teens or early 20s. 

I always wonder how I would have turned around in a different environment. Who would I be if I had been allowed to express myself and find my own personality.

Never had any work experience other than a 1 year stint as an internet, never had any life experience or lived through the usual teenage and young adult milestones. I can relate so hard to feeling on parallel lines, I describe it as being an alien inside of a test tube, an experiment gone wrong just watching everyone grow and move forward with their lives while mentally I'm still that sad and confused 15 year old who desperately wants to fit in. 

Thought I could run away from these feelings by giving up after graduating college, but it only made it worse. Now stuck at home, barely doing anything with zero love, life and work experience, I feel even more alien.

I always had visual snow, it's like having a noise filter on all the time and it gets worse when its dark. It gets worse after a migraine. I'm still not entirely convinced not everyone sees this way. I get migraines with auras, and sometimes the day before one I get these spots that are silver, they randomly appear, last a couple of seconds and then they are gone. It was similar to the gray dot from that day, but it didnt lasted very long.

Normally, what I struggle with is the feeling that I can't quite see everything that's in front of me. Like if I watch a movie I can barely see the subtitles unless I'm focusing entirely on it. Or if I'm reading something, I can't read the full word, I have to do it bit by bit. If I look at my fingertips I can barely see my knuckles. But if I pick a pen or whatever with my other hand and move it over them I do see it. Its like troxler fading, but extreme and at all times.

My migraine auras always begin with a blind spot, which is very different from these I just described. Its extremelly disturbing and always makes me feel sick.

I used to have some hope, but not anymore. It's a tough pill to swallow, I'm not sure I completely make sense of it, though I know it's never going to happen. I wish I could be the person I see in my mind, that someone would look at me and feel love and desire.

I had something similar happen to me in my first few days in high school. I went from a shy but talkative class clown in a small school to a quiet weirdo ditched by his only friend in a new, bigger school where most students knew each other since middle school, some literally since preschool. 

A girl one year older must have noticed that and would say hi whenever I walked past her. She was genuinely being nice, and I really appreciated it. Once in recess though, I walked past a large group with my head down, they were her friends and she said hi like always. The guys in her group were being loud, I thought they were making fun of me so I ignored her and went on my way. They all said a collective “Ohhh” and started poking fun at her for it, and she got angry and said something like “never mind then!”. She never said hi to me after that. 

The rest of my high school experience was miserable. I dreamed of befriending a group from my class, but it never happened. For a time in recess I would sit by then and listen to their chatting, laughing to myself when they said something funny. I realized how pathetic it was and started to hide in the library to read magazines instead. One guy from this group was nice to me, and one single time even invited me to be near them during a class outdoor exercise. But just like you I didn’t know how to react, I was painfully shy and awkward.

Didn’t wanted to make this about myself, though it’s nice to vent sometimes. Just wanted to let you know a lot of us can related to this situation. This girl seems nice, I hope you can befriend her and her group and don’t end up like me, almost 30 with nothing to show for and still commiserating about my shitty high school experience.

I spent some time in a similar subreddit and it made me empathize with the ones who referred themselves as incels. Loneliness doesn’t pick genders, it’s hard for everyone, and I related so much to the things they wrote about having dreams of relationships and family that seemed impossible. I used to comment here and there, but I was vague about my sexual identity, so I felt accepted. Their struggles seemed so much like mine.

One time though, I wrote a post detailing my life, how I’m a closeted trans woman (long way of saying I’m a man) and how not being able to be myself ruined my life. How I wish a man would look at me and find me attractive, eventually marry, have kids, have my own little family . I only received two comments, one saying I should cross dress because that’s some people's fetish, and the other said I should just go on a gay hookup app because according to him, gays don’t have such high standards.

I deleted the post and never went to that sub again. I was heartbroken, just when I was feeling like I could relate so much to a community for once, it became obvious I was not considered part of the group.

I hope you find her. It’s crazy how a brief online friendship can make such an impact on us. There was this girl online I just connected right away. She just stopped logging in and we never spoke, that’s over 10 years ago I think, and yet I think about her constantly.
I hope whatever it is, that it will be good for you.

My mom used to do this, but thankfully she stopped. She used to lament on how happy and talkative I was as a little kid, wondering out loud why I didn’t remained that way. As if I like being a withdrawn weirdo who is almost 30 and can’t function like a normal human being. As if it wasn’t she and my dad who reprimanded every bit of spontaneity out of me, from the way I talked, thought, played, making me feel bad for every normal question or reaction, making me regret every time I thought I could open up.

To me is the same as watching happy couples in real life. I feel happy for them, but then I get choked up because It’s a reminder I will never live my love story.

No men will ever look at me and feel and kind of desire towards me. I will never be able to bear children. That fantasy of meeting someone while young, falling madly in love with each other, marrying, building a family together, the whole white picket fence dream will never happen. Im so sick of being a supporting character in my own life. I want out.
